content: I’ll trace dyndep loading, depfile dependency recording, and dirty propagation, then add a focused regression test before running the narrow test suite.

The evidence supports a scan-order bug: the depfile-added `other` is visited as a source before the order-only `stamp` loads dyndep and assigns `other` its producer. I’m inspecting only the recomputation loop and dyndep edge update to place the minimal invalidation/revisit correctly.

Acceptance is now concrete: after all inputs have been traversed—and any ready dyndep files have mutated the graph—the parent edge must evaluate each input’s current producer readiness and dirty state. This preserves order-only semantics while eliminating the stale first-input decision. I’m applying that two-phase scan plus an in-memory regression matching the ready-dyndep/depfile/order-only case.

The patch transaction was rejected because the writer requires a complete read of `src/graph.cc` before replacing that loop. I’m satisfying that narrow precondition, then will apply the same supported change and run the focused test.

The writer’s complete-read check does not accept paginated or split reads as satisfying its safety precondition. The file is 813 lines, so I’m requesting that exact full range in one read before retrying.
The graph file now satisfies the precondition; the same check moved to the test file, which is larger. I’m completing its paginated read, then the single transaction can be applied and verified.
